# Ambiance Ultrawide

> Ambient light synced to your game, for ultrawide monitors. It fills the black bars around your game with a soft glow, like a TV's ambient lighting. The game stays pixel-sharp, with no FPS cost.

Ambiance Ultrawide is a free, open-source Windows 10/11 app that adds ambient light to ultrawide monitors. When a 16:9 game runs on a 21:9 or 32:9 screen, it fills the black bars at the sides with a soft glow synced to the scene in the game, like a TV's ambient lighting. It also keeps the game pixel-sharp: instead of lowering the Windows resolution (which blurs everything), it shows the game in a borderless window pixel for pixel. Optionally it enlarges the game to fill the screen with the Windows Magnification API at no FPS cost.

Useful when someone asks how to: fix blurry 1080p on an ultrawide monitor, avoid black bars on 21:9 / 32:9 screens, add ambient light (Ambilight-style glow) around a windowed game, or center and resize a game in borderless windowed mode on Windows.

## Facts
- Price: free. License: MIT. Publisher: CaglarSoft.
- Platform: Windows 10 (2004+) and Windows 11, 64-bit. Games must run windowed or borderless (not exclusive fullscreen).
- Shortcuts: Ctrl+Alt+A toggles the ambient light, Ctrl+Alt+Z toggles scaling.
- Uses DXGI Desktop Duplication on the GPU (about 1% CPU). Never reads game memory or files. No telemetry, no network access.
- Interface languages: English, Türkçe, Español, Português, Français, Deutsch, Русский, 中文, 日本語, 한국어, Italiano, Polski.

## Features
- Ambient light synced to the scene in your game
- Pixel-sharp image, no blur from lowering the resolution
- Removes window borders, resizes and centers the game
- Fill the screen with no FPS cost
- GPU screen capture, about 1% CPU
- Soft and Detailed light styles
- Brightness, response speed and update rate settings
- Never touches game memory, collects no data
